newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse rises on banks' gains, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse rises on banks' gains, seen up.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse rose in lower turnover pushed mainly by banks' strong performance and analysts said likely further gains of the recent uderperformers might lead to another growth at least on Friday.

The main market's WIG index rose 61.1 points or 0.4 percent, to 16,283.5, and turnover fell seven percent to 177.7 million zlotys ($57.3 million) on all three markets as 62 issues rose, 16 fell and 20 were flat.

Analysts said, however, banks' earnings prospects for 1997 were weak, after unspectacular first quarter, and said their current gains were only a reaction to an average 30-percent drop in the last three months.
"The engines of current growth are banks, but I can't see many reasons to make them rise much longer," said Janusz Oleksak, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

Analysts said a drop in year-on-year inflation to 15.3-percent in April, a figure reported on Thursday, was a good sign, but expected its moderate impact on the market as they saw no room for a rate cut before late in June.
They said in longer-term the bourse should extend its eight-week sideways drift as forthcoming elections and large privatisations were cooling demand.
All banks rose on Thursday with Kredyt Bank up 6.3 percent, PPABank and WBK jumping 5.9 percent each, BPH 4.6 percent, Bank Komunalny 3.8 percent, BRE 3.2 percent and Bank Slaski 2.9 percent.
Analysts said it was difficult to explain industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim 9.7-percent fall.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 0.7 percent to 156 zlotys ($50.3) in a 29.4-million-zloty ($9.5) turnover at the regular session but fell to 154 zlotys ($49.7) in later continuous trade.
